concepts.name: Algebraic expressions, terms and the degree of a polynomial
concepts.description: Terms, variables, coefficients and constants of an expression; one-variable (univariate) polynomials and their degree.
concepts.idea: A polynomial in one variable is an expression built from powers of that variable; its highest power is its degree.
concepts.rule: In 4x + 5y + 3 the terms are 4x, 5y and 3, the coefficients are 4 and 5, the constant is 3. The highest power of the variable is the degree: 1 linear, 2 quadratic, 3 cubic, 0 constant.
concepts.example: 5y^3 + y^2 + 2y - 1 has degree 3 (a cubic); coefficient of y^3 is 5, of y^2 is 1, of y is 2, constant term -1.

concepts.name: Linear polynomials, their values and linear equations
concepts.description: A degree-1 polynomial, finding its value by substitution (input-output view), and forming and solving linear equations from word problems.
concepts.idea: A linear polynomial gives one output for every input value of x; equating it to a number gives a linear equation.
concepts.rule: Value of a polynomial: substitute the number for the variable. To form an equation, let the unknown be x, write both sides and solve by inverse operations.
concepts.example: The sum of two numbers is 64 and one is 10 more than the other: x + (x + 10) = 64, so x = 27 and the numbers are 27 and 37.

concepts.name: Linear patterns
concepts.description: Sequences with a constant difference between consecutive terms, and finding the nth term as a linear expression in n.
concepts.idea: If each stage of a pattern adds the same amount, the nth term is a linear expression in n.
concepts.rule: A linear pattern has a constant difference d between consecutive terms. Tiles 1, 3, 5, 7, ... give the nth term 2n - 1.
concepts.example: Bela has 100 rupees and spends 5 rupees a day, so the amount on the nth day is 100 - 5n.

concepts.name: Linear growth and linear decay
concepts.description: Modelling situations where a quantity increases or decreases by a fixed amount over equal intervals with a linear function.
concepts.idea: Linear growth adds a fixed amount each interval; linear decay subtracts a fixed amount each interval.
concepts.rule: C(d) = 100 + 60d is growth (+60 per km); h(t) = 3 - 0.5t is decay (-0.5 per month).
concepts.example: A tank with 3 m of water loses 0.5 m a month: after 4 months h = 3 - 0.5 x 4 = 1 m.

concepts.name: Linear relationships y = ax + b
concepts.description: Finding the constants a and b of a linear relationship from two known pairs of values.
concepts.idea: In y = ax + b, a is the change in y for one unit of x and b is the value of y when x = 0.
concepts.rule: Substitute the two known pairs into y = ax + b, giving two equations, and solve for a and b.
concepts.example: A bill is 350 for 10 GB and 550 for 20 GB: 350 = 10a + b and 550 = 20a + b give a = 20, b = 150, so y = 20x + 150.

concepts.name: Graphs of linear equations: slope and y-intercept
concepts.description: Plotting y = ax + b as a straight line, and reading the slope a and the y-intercept b; parallel lines.
concepts.idea: The graph of y = ax + b is a straight line; a says how steep it is and b tells where it cuts the y-axis.
concepts.rule: y = ax + b has slope a and y-intercept b, cutting the y-axis at (0, b). y = ax passes through the origin. Equal slopes with different intercepts are parallel. Positive slope is growth; negative slope is decay.
concepts.example: y = 2x + 5 cuts the y-axis at (0, 5); y = 2x + 1 is parallel to it and cuts at (0, 1).
